title: FDAIMC: A Fully-Differential Analog In-Memory-Computing for MAC in MRAM with Accuracy Calibration Under Process and Voltage Variation
problem: STT-MRAM's low on/off ratio degrades analog in-memory-computing (AIMC) performance; process/voltage variation introduces unpredictable computation errors; incompatibility between analog and digital signals hinders calibration.
motivation: MRAM offers non-volatile storage with potential for energy-efficient compute, but analog computing on MRAM faces accuracy and reliability challenges across PVT corners.
method: Proposes fully-differential STT-MRAM AIMC macro with: (1) 2-level differential cell array and linear computing scheme with analog-domain calibration; (2) analog-digital conversion system including slew-rate-independent voltage-to-time converter (SRIVTC) and self-triggered time-to-MAC converter (STTMC); (3) compact layout for area efficiency. Calibration strategy adapts to process/voltage corners.
key_novelty: Fully-differential analog architecture with in-domain calibration and mixed-signal converters that bridge analog nonlinearity and digital linearity without specialized ADC hardware.
contributions: 95.44% accuracy in TT corner; 97.8% with calibration at FF; 88.6% at SS with >30% enhancement
1.64-21.18x area figure-of-merit vs state of the art
Slew-rate-independent converter and self-triggered MAC value converter
limitations: Evaluation limited to standard workloads; applicability to large-scale neural networks and mixed-precision computation not discussed.
primary_theme: fully-differential STT-MRAM AIMC with PVT calibration
